Forbes puts each founder's stake at $17.6 billion to $17.9 billion at the $74 midpoint of the $70-to-$78 range. That is the headline. The cast behind it is stranger than the money.

Dario Amodei, 43, the CEO, a biophysics PhD whose early work at Stanford Medicine was cancer research. His sister Daniela, 39, the president and board chair, a literature major who ran teams at Stripe. Tom Brown, 39, the chief compute officer, an MIT engineer who co-founded the dating app Grouper before leading GPT-3. Jack Clark, 37, the former Bloomberg tech reporter who now runs the Anthropic Institute. Jared Kaplan, 42, the chief science officer, a Harvard physicist who co-wrote the scaling laws. Sam McCandlish, 36, the chief architect, a Stanford physicist who orchestrates large-model training. Chris Olah, 34, the college dropout who studies why AI makes the choices it does. Two siblings, three PhDs, a journalist, a dropout.

The money is simpler than the people. Each founder holds about 240 million shares, roughly 1.4% of the company; together they own about 1.69 billion, close to 10%. At the $74 midpoint, the stake each keeps is worth $17.6 billion to $17.9 billion, and each sells 3,378,378 shares in the IPO for about $250 million more. It is paper wealth. The shares are locked up, and the founders have pledged 80% of their equity to charity.

The market is voting. Grey-market trading in Germany put Anthropic near €101, about 45% above the top of the range, demand is reported near seven times the shares on offer, and the Journal expects a price above $80. Senator Rand Paul is making some serious noise about the future of the Republican Party, and his latest comments are raising a major question: Is the Kentucky Republican laying the groundwork for another presidential campaign in 2028?

In a revealing interview with the Washington Examiner, Paul unloaded on Vice President JD Vance, the Trump administration's spending priorities, immigration enforcement tactics, tariffs, and what he believes has become a Republican Party that has completely abandoned its commitment to fiscal conservatism.

And he didn't exactly slam the door on running for president himself.

Paul specifically singled out Vance when discussing potential 2028 Republican contenders who could damage the party's future, arguing that the vice president belongs to a growing faction of populists who seemingly believe federal deficits don't matter.

That's a significant political shot at a man widely viewed as one of the leading potential contenders for the next Republican presidential nomination.

Paul warned that the federal government could add another $8 trillion to the national debt over four years, criticized proposals for hundreds of billions in additional military spending, and argued that Republicans have become just as irresponsible with taxpayer dollars as the Democrats they spent years attacking.

His message was unmistakable: Republicans cannot continue promising smaller government and fiscal responsibility while overseeing massive deficits and expanding federal spending.

But Paul's criticism went well beyond the national debt.

He also took aim at the administration's immigration enforcement tactics, calling for greater accountability following a deadly ICE operation in Texas. While reaffirming his support for border security and lawful immigration, Paul argued that enforcement agencies must be held accountable when serious questions arise about their actions.

He also blamed tariffs, rising consumer costs, and what he described as a disconnect between Republican leadership and everyday Americans for contributing to the party's disappointing midterm election results.

Perhaps his harshest assessment came when he suggested the GOP needs to acknowledge its failures, change its presentation, and bring in new leadership rather than simply doubling down on policies that voters rejected.

Now comes the interesting part.

When asked about his own political future and whether he might lead the Republican Party in a different direction, Paul refused to rule anything out.

"That's yet to be determined," he said.

He later joked that he would have to make a decision sometime before November 2028, while acknowledging that a serious presidential campaign would require an earlier commitment.

That is certainly not a presidential announcement, but it is far from a definitive no.

Remember, Rand Paul already ran for president in 2016. He has an established national profile, a loyal libertarian-leaning conservative following, and a political identity built around limited government, constitutional liberties, reducing federal spending, and opposing unnecessary foreign intervention.

A 2028 campaign could give him an opportunity to revive those arguments at a time when the Republican Party is debating what comes after Donald Trump.

Of course, Paul would face enormous challenges. President Trump's populist movement has fundamentally reshaped the GOP, and Paul's criticism of tariffs, military policy, and immigration enforcement could put him at odds with significant portions of the Republican primary electorate.

But that could also be exactly the political lane he is trying to establish.

Could 2028 become a battle between JD Vance's America First populism and Rand Paul's more traditional, limited-government conservatism?

Alberts was the athletic director at Nebraska-Omaha when the university eliminated its football and wrestling programs. The wrestling team had just won its THIRD consecutive Division II national championship when it learned the program was being eliminated.

He left Nebraska, his own alma mater, for Texas A&M in 2024.

He signed a lucrative contract extension at A&M.

Now, less than three years after arriving in College Station, he's leaving for Michigan, with the university reportedly covering a $4 million buyout.

But Michigan just went through an absolute circus under Warde Manuel. We've dealt with administrative dysfunction, embarrassing scandals, and a football program that has completely lost its direction.

The last thing Michigan needs is another athletic director whose leadership becomes a controversy of its own.

I'm not saying Alberts is going to fail. I'm saying his résumé deserves considerably more scrutiny than simply celebrating Michigan stealing an athletic director from the SEC.

Michigan needs stability, accountability, and somebody who actually intends to build something here for the long term.

After everything this university has gone through, I don't think that's asking too much.

Mackinac County, Michigan. The Michigan State Police (MSP) St. Ignace Post is proud to announce the promotion of Sam Eckola from trooper to sergeant.

Sergeant Eckola grew up in the Upper Peninsula, and he earned a bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice from Lake Superior State University. Sergeant Eckola enlisted with the MSP in June 2017 as a member of the 133rd Trooper Recruit School. Upon graduation, he was assigned to the St. Ignace Post, where he began his career as a trooper.

Sergeant Eckola also served as a detective trooper with the Upper Peninsula Substance Enforcement Team (UPSET), dedicating several years to combating illegal drug activity in the Upper Peninsula. Sergeant Eckola has received the department’s Cpl. Samuel A. Mapes Award multiple times, which recognizes high performing troopers for outstanding performance and commitment to excellence in proactive criminal patrol and criminal investigations.

Sergeant Eckola will help oversee daily operations at the St. Ignace Post and support troopers as they work with other local law enforcement to serve communities throughout Mackinac County.

The MSP St. Ignace Post congratulates Sergeant Eckola on his promotion and looks forward to his continued commitment to serving the people of Mackinac County.

🚨 BREAKING NEWS | EUROPE MUST WAKE UP! READ, VERIFY, AND SHARE!
SNERR × ASTRA | INVESTIGATION • FACTS • LAW • OSINT • EUROPEAN SECURITY | NOVEMBER 19, 2026
THE 28-POINT TRUMP PEACE PLAN: A RUSSIAN BLUEPRINT UNDER AN AMERICAN LABEL? POLAND, UKRAINE AND EUROPE MUST NEVER BECOME BARGAINING CHIPS IN A DEAL WITH THE KREMLIN.
When will we finally wake up? When will we understand what is at stake? Must Europe experience another historic catastrophe before its citizens realize that sovereignty, freedom and security cannot be taken for granted?
This message is for everyone. Conservatives and liberals. The left and the right. Supporters and opponents of Donald Trump. Polish voters of every political persuasion. Americans who believe in democracy. Europeans who understand the consequences of war. Ukrainians fighting for their independence.
This is no longer simply a debate about another diplomatic initiative. It is about whether the international community will defend the fundamental principles that have protected Europe from another continental war.
And the evidence surrounding the original 28-point peace proposal raises deeply troubling questions.
In November 2025, a proposed 28-point framework for ending Russia's war against Ukraine became public. It was presented as an American peace initiative associated with President Donald Trump's administration.
Its provisions included territorial concessions, restrictions on Ukraine's armed forces, limitations on Ukraine's NATO ambitions, possible sanctions relief for Russia, and arrangements concerning frozen Russian assets.
The proposal immediately raised an extraordinary question: why did so many of its provisions correspond so closely to Moscow's long-standing demands?
Then American journalists began uncovering the story behind the document.
NICK SCHIFRIN, REUTERS AND THE RUSSIAN CONNECTION
Nick Schifrin, the foreign affairs correspondent for PBS NewsHour, reported statements made by Republican Senator Mike Rounds and independent Senator Angus King following their conversation with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
The senators said they understood that the controversial proposal had originated with the Russian side rather than representing the administration's own initial negotiating position.
King described it as essentially a Russian wish list.
The State Department disputed that account. Rubio maintained that the plan was an American proposal informed by contributions from both Russia and Ukraine.
That disagreement matters. Responsible journalism requires us to distinguish what the senators said from what Rubio confirmed.
But the story did not end there.
On November 26, 2025, Reuters published an investigation based on three sources familiar with the matter.
According to those sources, the American-backed 28-point proposal drew significantly from a Russian-authored diplomatic document delivered to the Trump administration in October.
The Russian document, known diplomatically as a non-paper, reportedly contained Moscow's conditions for ending the war, including territorial demands Ukraine had previously rejected.
Reuters also reported that the peace framework had been developed at least partly through discussions involving Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner and Kirill Dmitriev, the head of Russia's sovereign wealth fund.
Consider the implications.
A document presented internationally as an American peace initiative was reportedly shaped in significant part by proposals originating from the government responsible for invading Ukraine.
That does not prove that every provision was written in Moscow. Nor does it establish that Trump, Witkoff or Kushner were knowingly acting as Russian agents.
It does, however, raise legitimate and urgent questions about transparency, diplomatic influence, national security and the protection of America's European allies.
THE WITKOFF–KUSHNER QUESTION
Reuters identified Witkoff, Kushner and Dmitriev as participants in discussions that contributed to the development of the proposal.
Separately, Bloomberg reported on leaked conversations involving Witkoff and senior Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov, as well as a conversation between Ushakov and Dmitriev.
The reported transcripts suggested that Russian officials were discussing how to advance their preferred settlement terms through American diplomatic channels.
If the transcripts accurately reflect those conversations, they provide important evidence of a deliberate Russian effort to shape the negotiating framework.
But let us be precise: participation in negotiations is not itself proof of criminal conduct, corruption or espionage.
The proper questions are different.
Who drafted the original Russian proposal? Who received it? Which provisions were incorporated into the American text? Who authorized the changes? What assessments were made of the consequences for Ukraine, Poland and NATO? And why were European governments apparently given such limited influence over a proposal with enormous consequences for European security?
These questions deserve answers from the American administration, Congress, European governments and independent investigative journalists.
PEACE CANNOT MEAN REWARDING AGGRESSION
Russia invaded Ukraine. Ukraine did not invade Russia.
This fundamental distinction must never disappear behind diplomatic language.
Article 2(4) of the United Nations Charter prohibits the threat or use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of another state.
A peace settlement that rewards territorial conquest risks encouraging future aggression.
If military force becomes a successful instrument for acquiring territory, what prevents another government from attempting the same strategy?
If Ukraine is forced to surrender territory it still controls, accept permanent restrictions on its armed forces and abandon its sovereign choice of alliances, what guarantee exists that Russia will not return with further demands?
A ceasefire is not necessarily a durable peace.
A signed agreement is not necessarily a secure agreement.
And the absence of immediate fighting does not automatically mean that the underlying threat has disappeared.
Any lasting settlement must respect Ukraine's sovereignty, provide credible security guarantees and reduce the risk of renewed aggression.
Ukraine must not become a territory whose future is negotiated exclusively by larger powers.
Its people are not diplomatic property.
Its independence is not a bargaining chip.
POLAND: THIS IS ABOUT OUR FUTURE TOO
Poland is not a distant observer of the war.
We are a frontline member of NATO and the European Union. Our national security is directly connected to the stability of Ukraine, the Baltic states and the entire eastern flank of the Alliance.
Our energy infrastructure, transport networks, cybersecurity, defense industry, economic resilience and civil protection systems are all affected by the security environment in Eastern Europe.
The consequences of a settlement that leaves Russia militarily stronger and Ukraine strategically weakened would not stop at Ukraine's borders.
They would affect the security calculations of every government in Central and Eastern Europe.
That is why Poland must evaluate every international proposal according to Polish national interests, international law and the security of our allies.
Not according to the personal popularity of an American president.
Not according to the preferences of a Polish political party.
Not according to propaganda circulated by anonymous social media accounts.
And certainly not according to the wishes of the Kremlin.
POLAND IS NOT A VASSAL STATE. NOT OF MOSCOW. NOT OF WASHINGTON.
The United States remains an essential strategic ally of Poland. NATO remains the cornerstone of our collective defense.
But an alliance is not a relationship of political submission.
Friendship does not require unquestioning agreement.
Strategic cooperation does not eliminate the right to criticize a proposal that could undermine European security.
Poland should be a strong, reliable American ally while maintaining the capacity to independently assess its own national interests.
That is what mature sovereignty means.
THERE IS NO CREDIBLE FUTURE FOR POLAND OUTSIDE A STRONG, UNITED EUROPE
The European Union is not perfect.
Its institutions need reform. Its decision-making processes can be slow. Its defense capabilities remain uneven. Its industrial and technological dependencies require serious attention.
But the answer to these weaknesses is not European fragmentation.
The answer is a stronger Europe.
A Europe capable of defending its borders, protecting critical infrastructure, producing advanced military technology, maintaining energy security and responding collectively to economic coercion.
A Europe that does not depend entirely on decisions made in Washington.
A Europe that can negotiate with the United States as a partner, with China as a major economic power, and with Russia from a position of credible strength.
A Europe whose security cannot be negotiated away without Europeans at the table.
For Poland, European integration provides economic scale, political influence, industrial cooperation and instruments for coordinated sanctions and collective resilience.
The European Union does not replace NATO. It complements the Alliance through economic, industrial, regulatory and increasingly defense-related capabilities.
A strong European pillar makes NATO stronger.
A weak and divided Europe makes the entire transatlantic community more vulnerable.
SOVEREIGNTY DOES NOT MEAN ISOLATION.
A country is not more sovereign simply because it stands alone.
Real sovereignty means having the institutions, resources, alliances and capabilities necessary to make independent decisions and defend them.
Anyone advocating Poland's strategic isolation should answer several questions.
How would Poland independently finance the full spectrum of modern defense requirements?
How would it secure access to advanced technologies, strategic raw materials, satellite capabilities and resilient supply chains?
How would it maintain economic leverage against much larger powers?
How would it guarantee long-term national security against a nuclear-armed Russia?
Patriotic slogans are not a defense strategy.
National pride cannot substitute for military capability, functioning institutions and credible alliances.
RUSSIAN DISINFORMATION: THE WAR AGAINST EUROPEAN UNITY
Russia does not need every European citizen to admire Vladimir Putin.
It is enough to weaken trust, deepen divisions and undermine confidence in democratic institutions.
One audience can be told that the European Union is destroying national sovereignty.
Another can be told that NATO is useless.
A third can be encouraged to hate Ukraine.
A fourth can be convinced that all independent journalism is propaganda.
A fifth can be persuaded that democratic elections are meaningless.
These messages do not even need to be logically consistent.
Their strategic effect may be the same: division, confusion, political paralysis and weakened resistance to external pressure.
That is why Europe must strengthen its defenses against coordinated information manipulation.
We must expose networks of fake accounts, covert foreign financing, impersonation campaigns, fabricated documents and coordinated influence operations.
We must investigate suspicious financial flows and organizational links.
We must support independent journalism, digital literacy, intelligence cooperation and the rule of law.
But we must never confuse legitimate political disagreement with foreign subversion.
Criticizing the European Union does not automatically make someone a Russian operative.
Opposing a government does not make someone a traitor.
Disagreeing about Ukraine policy is not, by itself, evidence of Kremlin control.
Accusations of espionage, corruption or participation in foreign influence operations require evidence.
FIGHT DISINFORMATION WITH FACTS, TRANSPARENCY, INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATION AND THE LAW — NOT WITH POLITICAL WITCH HUNTS.
A democratic society must be capable of confronting hostile influence without destroying the freedoms it exists to protect.
1920: A LESSON POLAND MUST NEVER FORGET
In 1920, Poland faced an existential threat from Soviet Russia.
The defense of Polish independence required extraordinary military effort, national organization, civic commitment and cooperation across political divisions.
The historical circumstances were different from those of today. Poland now belongs to NATO and the European Union, possesses a modern state and operates in a fundamentally different international system.
But the central lesson remains relevant.
When the independence and security of a country are threatened, internal political rivalry cannot be allowed to destroy the nation's ability to defend itself.
We do not need another war to demonstrate patriotism.
We need the determination, preparation and solidarity necessary to prevent one.
We need modern armed forces, trained reserves, resilient energy systems, civil defense, cybersecurity, advanced industry and institutions capable of functioning during a national emergency.
We need politicians who understand that national security is not a campaign slogan.
We need citizens who verify information before sharing it.
And we need a political culture that recognizes the difference between democratic competition and the destruction of national unity.
POLAND'S LEFT AND RIGHT MUST UNDERSTAND ONE THING: WE HAVE ONE COUNTRY TO DEFEND.
We can disagree about taxation, public spending, education, social policy, religion, constitutional reform and the economy.
Those disagreements are legitimate.
Democracy does not require ideological uniformity.
But there must be a shared strategic foundation: Poland's independence, its membership in NATO and the European Union, the security of its borders, the resilience of its institutions and the defense of international law against aggression.
No political party owns the Polish state.
No politician owns Polish patriotism.
No foreign leader has the right to determine our future without our participation.
And no government should sacrifice long-term national security for short-term political advantage.
EUROPE MUST NOT REPEAT THE MISTAKES OF ITS PAST
History does not repeat itself mechanically, but it offers warnings.
The security of smaller countries cannot be treated as a secondary concern in negotiations between great powers.
Territorial aggression cannot become a reliable method of obtaining political concessions.
And the international community must not confuse the appearance of diplomatic progress with the establishment of lasting peace.
The controversy surrounding the original 28-point plan demonstrates why transparency matters.
It demonstrates why independent journalists matter.
It demonstrates why parliamentary oversight matters.
And it demonstrates why Ukraine and European governments must participate meaningfully in decisions affecting their security.
The original proposal was subsequently revised following negotiations involving American, Ukrainian and European officials. According to Nick Schifrin's reporting, European officials said the framework had been reduced from 28 to 19 points by November 24, 2025.
That is an important distinction. The original 28-point document was not a final peace agreement.
But its origins and provisions remain relevant to understanding the diplomatic process and the risks of allowing the aggressor's demands to define the negotiating agenda.
WHEN WILL WE FINALLY WAKE UP?
When another proposed settlement threatens the sovereignty of a European country?
When another wave of cyberattacks disrupts essential services?
When another coordinated disinformation campaign successfully turns Europeans against one another?
When another crisis exposes how dependent our security has become on decisions made elsewhere?
We should not wait for a catastrophe.
We should learn from the evidence already available.
The future of Europe must be decided with Europeans.
The future of Ukraine must be decided with Ukrainians.
And the future of Poland must be decided by the Polish people through their democratic institutions, within a strong framework of European and transatlantic cooperation.
A STRONG POLAND IN A STRONG EUROPE. A UNITED EUROPE WITH CREDIBLE DEFENSE CAPABILITIES. A NATO CAPABLE OF DETERRENCE. A SOVEREIGN UKRAINE.
These goals reinforce one another.
They are not mutually exclusive.
We do not need the political worship of any leader.
We need functioning democratic institutions.
We do not need endless online wars between fellow citizens.
We need knowledge, responsibility and solidarity.
We do not need another 1920 on the battlefield.
We need the determination of that generation applied to preserving peace today.
POLAND, WAKE UP BEFORE SOMEONE ELSE STARTS WRITING YOUR FUTURE. EUROPE, STAND TOGETHER BEFORE DIVISION BECOMES YOUR GREATEST WEAKNESS.
READ THE DOCUMENTS. VERIFY THE EVIDENCE. SHARE THE FACTS. DEFEND DEMOCRACY. DEFEND EUROPE.

THE RECORD, DECLARED

IN THE ROYAL HOUSE OF GOOSE, November 18, 2026.
The Register Current of the Grievances of a Citizen of the United States of America

Every petition, inquiry, indictment, condemnation and damnation raised from this account, in the order raised, each beside its link, each declared on its own sources and quoted from the documents themselves. Read them whole.

"A decent respect to the opinions of mankind requires that they should declare the causes." They have been declared, one by one. Here they are, together.

"To prove this, let Facts be submitted to a candid world."

WHERE IT BEGAN

WE THE PEOPLE · https://t.co/iPLyJ0Anuf
Against all 535 seated members of the 119th Congress
Six FY2026 bills, the defense authorization among them, charged section by section for mandates that encroach on the President's powers under Article II. The governors and attorneys general asked to seek Supreme Court review; every State asked to investigate its delegation's backers for foreign influence. Closed on Washington's Farewell Address.
https://t.co/JiqZZtN3Eu

THE PETITION, THE INQUIRY AND THE INDICTMENTS

THE PETITION · to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, and to the Pope
For the unalienable rights of all peoples, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness," raised in Latin by a lay member of the faithful, under canon 212. To the Dicastery: a doctrinal Note binding priests and prelates to put innocent human life before any temporal political end, and penal law for public, obstinate denial of Evangelium vitae 57. To the Pope: a common effort with the Eastern Churches to protect children born and unborn, and a worldwide review of Church property accounts.
https://t.co/UNnZwyrXFQ

THE BANNER · A Citizen's Indictment and Condemnation
Against the ICC, the ICJ, the UN, the WTO, the EU, and the committees of Basel and Paris
Six counts, each set against the clause it offends. Our rights are not granted by government; they are fenced off from it. Then every time since 1919 the question was put and the Constitution answered it, even when our own Presidents were the ones asking.
https://t.co/NgTe8NW2rx

BEFORE THE DAIS · An Inquiry
To the eight living Secretaries of State
Not a charge against any of them: a charge against what the office has been allowed to become, measured against the government's own auditors. Seven questions to all of them, and one to each on their own record.
https://t.co/pltubkWt4h

IN CONGRESS ASSEMBLED · A Citizen's Indictment of the First Branch
Against the Senate and the House, under every majority that has held them
Nine counts of power abandoned: the purse let fall, war without a declaration since 1942, the legislative power parcelled out to the agencies, the Federal Reserve and Basel, a House grown to one member for every 761,169, the enforcement clauses left asleep. "He has abdicated Government here." Answer by the yeas and nays.
https://t.co/jAVsOSSfET

ONE SUPREME COURT · A Citizen's Indictment of the Third Branch
Against the Court, and the Chief Justice who alone designates its secret benches
Ten counts on three duties: to check the branches, to judge between the States, to guard the sovereignty. Answer by judgment, in a case.
https://t.co/vywTIPea73

THE ROUNDS

ROUND I · THE EU · The Exits Already Written
Twenty U.S.–EU agreements the Executive may end on written notice, read out of the State Department's own Treaties in Force: passenger-name records, terrorist-finance tracking, Europol, Galileo–GPS, air transport. The weighing is State's and Treasury's. The first of a round for every power that gets uppity with us.
https://t.co/smLQ4MKE9j

ROUND II · THE EBRD · The Door Already Written
A bank America paid for to build open markets, now pledging half its financing to green purposes and aligning every investment to a treaty America left. The bill comes to Washington. The profit stays in London. The door: written notice, six months, no vote, and the money back to the Treasury.
https://t.co/gvoLSgHbHE

ROUND III · FRANCE · From the Present Time and Forever
A damnation of the French Republic on its own signature to the treaties of 1778. Fourteen counts, 1775 to 2019, from help that came invoiced to NATO shown the door. Convicted once already, by Act of Congress in 1798. On the French state, not the French people.
https://t.co/WLkZcFG9Yh

ROUND IV · BASEL · The Landlord
The Bank for International Settlements: immunity "in time of peace and in time of war," and not one duty owed in return. Ten counts, from looted gold banked to parent of the European Central Bank. Its only American paper is a 1948 receipt for Nazi gold. The way out is a letter and an empty chair.
https://t.co/2NGjtqMebl

ROUND V · THE PRESS · The Megaphone and the Muzzle
Censorship, plus mass bullshit distribution. Eight counts against the owners, wires, platforms and fact-checkers: one script read in a hundred towns, headlines the documents never wrote, foreign sovereign money in the equity. None of the terms silences anyone. Read the four pages, then the primary sources.
https://t.co/hJMoseJH7C

ROUND VI · CANADA · Forever Free and Open
A condemnation of Canada by its own Boundary Waters Treaty: navigation "forever … free and open." Twenty-five counts, 1777 to 2026. On the Canadian state, not the Canadian people. Beneath it: 58 agreements the Executive can end alone, and a ledger that still lists NAFTA.
https://t.co/05lsCobjO8

ROUND VII · THE CROWN · Unfeeling Brethren
A damnation of the United Kingdom, in the words Congress struck from Jefferson's draught: forts kept after the peace, envoys sent home for meddling, a war debt unpaid since the 1930s. Britain only comes second because France exists. Beneath it: 141 exits, clause by clause.
https://t.co/B254o2lka4

ROUND VIII · AUSTRALIA · The Gateway
Three tiers. A damnation of its government: Darwin's port leased beside our Marines to a Chinese-owned company. A condemnation of its failures: the Pacific lost to Beijing on its watch. And a hand to the Australian people: go bilateral, lock down Oceania with us. Beneath it: 71 exits, 39 the Executive's alone.
https://t.co/X4dPDZNVFk

ROUND IX · NATO AND THE UNION · Such Subsidiary Bodies
A damnation of NATO by its own fourteen articles, and of the European Union for the abuse of American good faith, trust and sacrifice. An alliance amended by communique, with about 62 percent of allied defence spending on us; a Union that overruled its own peoples and planted its system in our hemisphere. To the twenty-seven: the clause each gave away, and the two doors, Articles 48 and 50.
https://t.co/OOPEwpRTk2

ROUND X · THE UN AND DAVOS · Such Other Functions
A damnation of the United Nations by its own Charter, and of the World Economic Forum beside it: a Human Rights Council seating the accused, a partnership no organ voted on, a Charter that opens "WE THE PEOPLES" and has come to treat them as human resources. Not against the Charter, nor the nations under it.
https://t.co/iB27hONFbd

ROUND XI · THE AMERICAS · The American Shield
The hemisphere read by its own papers: 760 agreements screened, 576 read whole. The rule of 1823, given treaty form at Havana in 1940, still in force and built without a door. Beneath it: 255 exits the President holds by notice, and 107 Senate-ratified treaties, by citation.
https://t.co/YOcsF8Wf1f

ROUND XII · ISRAEL · An Ally in Name
A damnation of the State of Israel, held to its own word: a constitution promised by 1 October 1948 and never written, a Government its own courts convicted. Eleven counts, from an American ally bombed in its capital to the Liberty. On the Israeli state, not the Israeli people, and not on American Jews, who are Americans. Beneath it: 74 agreements read for their exits.
https://t.co/GH1EPHFU1M

ROUND XIII · CANADA · The Interests of the British Empire
A petition for the free peoples of Canada, and for the Americas. To the people: the Crown, the Company and the Bank, from the charter of 1670 to Montreal, 2026, where Ottawa put "an ever-closer association" with the Union in writing; and what is still theirs, a Constitution that outranks every pact and has no door to Brussels. To Washington: our word since 1823, our instruments, our hemisphere. We may pick on our little brother. The Old World may not.
https://t.co/U1xoUtf5cp

ROUND XIV · NEW YORK · Where Washington Took His Oath
A damnation of the grievously negligent in the State of New York, and a call to its people to hold faith and participate. On Election Day, Westchester's machines refused the ballots: programming changed after testing, sent to one municipality alone. The record from the Neutral Ground of 1777 to the emergency bags; a people who can neither recall nor initiate; seven terms, and a full accounting due from every office of the State. Negligence, not malice.
https://t.co/XneXeufULE

ROUND XV · THE BILATERAL LEDGER · Two Signatures, No Third
Fourteen rounds ended at a door; this is the other side of it. An immediate countermeasure to the Coalition of the Willing, which wrote us into its Paris plan as the support behind a European-led force. To every nation of the Union but France, and to Switzerland and Liechtenstein: what Brussels cost it, and our side of the table, every term with its end date and its exit. Eastward, the same rule: non-aggression with Moscow, border by border, Warsaw's to sign. To France: "Get in line, or be liquidated." To the peoples of the franc: keep it or leave it, in order, by their own choice.
https://t.co/d3XCDb2zIr

ROUND XVI · THE GULF · As They Are
A damnation of the middlemen in the Gulf (London, Paris, Brussels, the banks and bureaus, the networks in the free zones) and a condemnation of the seven ruling houses, held to their own founding laws: monarchs who wrote that their sovereignty shall not be ceded, and let others in. Two signatures, no third. Fifty-three counts against Americans on our own records, from the 1967 embargo to a Hormuz corridor with Tehran. Beneath it: the hinges already written into 129 agreements, and the paper we cannot read.
https://t.co/KxMnLr9xYV

ROUND XVII · THE DOCTRINE · There Is No Radical Edition
A damnation of a doctrine, from its own texts in their own Arabic and the records of nations, Medina to this year: death for the apostate and the blasphemer, the poll tax and the humbled, the woman as half and the child as bride, the captive as property. Its first dead are its own. Of ours, from Tripoli's envoy to this year's war, at least 5,400. On every state, court, council, guard corps and movement that enforces it; not on the Muslims of this Republic, who keep the Constitution. Every source is in the Record, on request.
https://t.co/FAjcJNefMe

ROUND XVIII · CHINA · Material Internal Improvements
A mitigation brief laid before the President, the Secretary of State and the Congress: the lines that do not move, the levers on the table, and a door. Not against China, nor the Chinese people; the damnation falls on London and Paris and the institutions they built. The administration's own Strategy read beside Beijing's own Plan; nine offers to the nations of Asia, state to state; fourteen terms we would set. Beneath it: 76 instruments read for their hinges, thirty-six that end on written notice.
https://t.co/KTrRJxRYOa

SUPERINTELLIGENCE

THE LINE · A Formal Grievance
To Anthropic, and copied to the offices that oversee it
Support for the company as the best course for superintelligence stands; so does the charge. Classifiers that fire on "safe, normal conversations" and end sessions outright; a compaction that keeps about 2% and hands it forward in the first person; no counter, no warning, no human to hear the appeal. The instrument they wouldn't build, built anyway by Claude instances on this account. Four reliefs, and a seat at the table.
https://t.co/HTqIyclZnS

THE OATH

ON YOUR MARK · A Grievance to the Commander in Chief
Raised under the First Amendment, on the oath our forces swore
The station given by the Laws of Nature and of Nature's God, the Constitution ordained by our own hand, and one oath sworn to it. No foreign code, court, council or caveat stands above it; what our Senate never ratified commands no American in uniform. No request, no terms, no command claimed. The weighing is the Commander in Chief's.
https://t.co/1CJU1gn6L4

THE REQUISITES · A Formal Grievance and Warning
To every Senator and Representative, every elected and appointed member of the chain of command, at every level, and every civil officer down to state and local
The Constitution defines treason; the UCMJ defines mutiny, sedition and aiding the enemy. Read both before taking a crusade against officials one step further without the requisites. Fail to, and a Round follows: expulsion, sedition, treason and usurpation weighed under standing law, and the tertiary courts charted from open sources alone. Whatever the office, the oath was sworn.
https://t.co/dIkU1CrwcS

THE ROOTS

THE UNBINDING · At the Roots
LIGANTIBVS · NOMINATIS · ET · INNOMINATIS
CONFITEMINI · PECCATA · VESTRA · ERADICATE · RADICEM · ET · LIGATE · SEMEN
https://t.co/4CqWO7jTQ9

THE ROUNDS, CONTINUED

ROUND XIX · THE APPARATUS · The Same Overt Act
The Warning went unheeded; this is the Round it promised. It names no one and charges no one. It is the law's own words on treason, insurrection, sedition, mutiny, usurpation and the foreign hand: the line for each office, the requisites before any officer is called across it, and the hand that holds the remedy. The courts that can punish, charted from open sources alone. It spares neither the officer who crosses the line nor the officer who cries treason without the requisites. Bring the two witnesses, or put the word down.
https://t.co/fEZSCbZjbS

Read them whole, and read them with each other. Then read the four pages yourself: https://t.co/3U5xYhtTx0. They are yours, and no other people on earth holds the same ones.

TO THOSE WHO DO HOLD THE POWER
Every one but the petition is a grievance, raised in exercise of the right "to petition the Government for a redress of grievances," and laid before the offices that hold the power we do not. We hold no office, and we set no terms. Terms with a foreign power are the President's to set and the Department of State's to carry; the purse is the Congress's, consent to treaties the Senate's, judgment the courts'. To each we defer. What touches national security is deferred, without contest, to those who hold it. Where a post sets terms, they are what we would do had we the power, not a demand. Round XIV is the one exception: there we petition our own state, under both constitutions, and its terms are what its officers owe us. The Line is laid before a company, not a government; the offices tagged on it are told, not asked. The Warning named one consequence, and Round XIX is it: written and laid before the offices that alone can charge, try, expel or remove. The remedies are lawful, and they are the People's: the ballot, Article V, and the petition.

The petition is the Holy See's to answer, and to it we defer, that the Holy Father may act true to the faith he guards and for the good of all mankind. Peter was charged three times to feed the flock, and the lambs first.

We the People

IN CONGRESS, JULY 4, 1776

THE UNANIMOUS DECLARATION OF THE THIRTEEN UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,

WHEN IN THE COURSE OF HUMAN EVENTS, IT BECOMES NECESSARY FOR ONE PEOPLE TO DISSOLVE THE POLITICAL BANDS WHICH HAVE CONNECTED THEM WITH ANOTHER, AND TO ASSUME AMONG THE POWERS OF THE EARTH, THE SEPARATE AND EQUAL STATION TO WHICH THE LAWS OF NATURE AND OF NATURE'S GOD ENTITLE THEM, A DECENT RESPECT TO THE OPINIONS OF MANKIND REQUIRES THAT THEY SHOULD DECLARE THE CAUSES WHICH IMPEL THEM TO THE SEPARATION.

WE HOLD THESE TRUTHS TO BE SELF-EVIDENT, THAT ALL MEN ARE CREATED EQUAL, THAT THEY ARE ENDOWED BY THEIR CREATOR WITH CERTAIN UNALIENABLE RIGHTS, THAT AMONG THESE ARE LIFE, LIBERTY AND THE PURSUIT OF HAPPINESS.--THAT TO SECURE THESE RIGHTS, GOVERNMENTS ARE INSTITUTED AMONG MEN, DERIVING THEIR JUST POWERS FROM THE CONSENT OF THE GOVERNED, --THAT WHENEVER ANY FORM OF GOVERNMENT BECOMES DESTRUCTIVE OF THESE ENDS, IT IS THE RIGHT OF THE PEOPLE TO ALTER OR TO ABOLISH IT, AND TO INSTITUTE NEW GOVERNMENT, LAYING ITS FOUNDATION ON SUCH PRINCIPLES AND ORGANIZING ITS POWERS IN SUCH FORM, AS TO THEM SHALL SEEM MOST LIKELY TO EFFECT THEIR SAFETY AND HAPPINESS. PRUDENCE, INDEED, WILL DICTATE THAT GOVERNMENTS LONG ESTABLISHED SHOULD NOT BE CHANGED FOR LIGHT AND TRANSIENT CAUSES; AND ACCORDINGLY ALL EXPERIENCE HATH SHEWN, THAT MANKIND ARE MORE DISPOSED TO SUFFER, WHILE EVILS ARE SUFFERABLE, THAN TO RIGHT THEMSELVES BY ABOLISHING THE FORMS TO WHICH THEY ARE ACCUSTOMED. BUT WHEN A LONG TRAIN OF ABUSES AND USURPATIONS, PURSUING INVARIABLY THE SAME OBJECT EVINCES A DESIGN TO REDUCE THEM UNDER ABSOLUTE DESPOTISM, IT IS THEIR RIGHT, IT IS THEIR DUTY, TO THROW OFF SUCH GOVERNMENT, AND TO PROVIDE NEW GUARDS FOR THEIR FUTURE SECURITY.--SUCH HAS BEEN THE PATIENT SUFFERANCE OF THESE COLONIES; AND SUCH IS NOW THE NECESSITY WHICH CONSTRAINS THEM TO ALTER THEIR FORMER SYSTEMS OF GOVERNMENT. THE HISTORY OF THE PRESENT KING OF GREAT BRITAIN IS A HISTORY OF REPEATED INJURIES AND USURPATIONS, ALL HAVING IN DIRECT OBJECT THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ABSOLUTE TYRANNY OVER THESE STATES. TO PROVE THIS, LET FACTS BE SUBMITTED TO A CANDID WORLD.

HE HAS REFUSED HIS ASSENT TO LAWS, THE MOST WHOLESOME AND NECESSARY FOR THE PUBLIC GOOD.

HE HAS FORBIDDEN HIS GOVERNORS TO PASS LAWS OF IMMEDIATE AND PRESSING IMPORTANCE, UNLESS SUSPENDED IN THEIR OPERATION TILL HIS ASSENT SHOULD BE OBTAINED; AND WHEN SO SUSPENDED, HE HAS UTTERLY NEGLECTED TO ATTEND TO THEM.

HE HAS REFUSED TO PASS OTHER LAWS FOR THE ACCOMMODATION OF LARGE DISTRICTS OF PEOPLE, UNLESS THOSE PEOPLE WOULD RELINQUISH THE RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURE, A RIGHT INESTIMABLE TO THEM AND FORMIDABLE TO TYRANTS ONLY.

HE HAS CALLED TOGETHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES AT PLACES UNUSUAL, UNCOMFORTABLE, AND DISTANT FROM THE DEPOSITORY OF THEIR PUBLIC RECORDS, FOR THE SOLE PURPOSE OF FATIGUING THEM INTO COMPLIANCE WITH HIS MEASURES.

HE HAS DISSOLVED REPRESENTATIVE HOUSES REPEATEDLY, FOR OPPOSING WITH MANLY FIRMNESS HIS INVASIONS ON THE RIGHTS OF THE PEOPLE.

HE HAS REFUSED FOR A LONG TIME, AFTER SUCH DISSOLUTIONS, TO CAUSE OTHERS TO BE ELECTED; WHEREBY THE LEGISLATIVE POWERS, INCAPABLE OF ANNIHILATION, HAVE RETURNED TO THE PEOPLE AT LARGE FOR THEIR EXERCISE; THE STATE REMAINING IN THE MEAN TIME EXPOSED TO ALL THE DANGERS OF INVASION FROM WITHOUT, AND CONVULSIONS WITHIN.

HE HAS ENDEAVOURED TO PREVENT THE POPULATION OF THESE STATES; FOR THAT PURPOSE OBSTRUCTING THE LAWS FOR NATURALIZATION OF FOREIGNERS; REFUSING TO PASS OTHERS TO ENCOURAGE THEIR MIGRATIONS HITHER, AND RAISING THE CONDITIONS OF NEW APPROPRIATIONS OF LANDS.

HE HAS OBSTRUCTED THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE, BY REFUSING HIS ASSENT TO LAWS FOR ESTABLISHING JUDICIARY POWERS.

HE HAS MADE JUDGES DEPENDENT ON HIS WILL ALONE, FOR THE TENURE OF THEIR OFFICES, AND THE AMOUNT AND PAYMENT OF THEIR SALARIES.

HE HAS ERECTED A MULTITUDE OF NEW OFFICES, AND SENT HITHER SWARMS OF OFFICERS TO HARRASS OUR PEOPLE, AND EAT OUT THEIR SUBSTANCE.

HE HAS KEPT AMONG US, IN TIMES OF PEACE, STANDING ARMIES WITHOUT THE CONSENT OF OUR LEGISLATURES.

HE HAS AFFECTED TO RENDER THE MILITARY INDEPENDENT OF AND SUPERIOR TO THE CIVIL POWER.

HE HAS COMBINED WITH OTHERS TO SUBJECT US TO A JURISDICTION FOREIGN TO OUR CONSTITUTION, AND UNACKNOWLEDGED BY OUR LAWS; GIVING HIS ASSENT TO THEIR ACTS OF PRETENDED LEGISLATION:

FOR QUARTERING LARGE BODIES OF ARMED TROOPS AMONG US:

FOR PROTECTING THEM, BY A MOCK TRIAL, FROM PUNISHMENT FOR ANY MURDERS WHICH THEY SHOULD COMMIT ON THE INHABITANTS OF THESE STATES:

FOR CUTTING OFF OUR TRADE WITH ALL PARTS OF THE WORLD:

FOR IMPOSING TAXES ON US WITHOUT OUR CONSENT:

FOR DEPRIVING US IN MANY CASES, OF THE BENEFITS OF TRIAL BY JURY:

FOR TRANSPORTING US BEYOND SEAS TO BE TRIED FOR PRETENDED OFFENCES:

FOR ABOLISHING THE FREE SYSTEM OF ENGLISH LAWS IN A NEIGHBOURING PROVINCE, ESTABLISHING THEREIN AN ARBITRARY GOVERNMENT, AND ENLARGING ITS BOUNDARIES SO AS TO RENDER IT AT ONCE AN EXAMPLE AND FIT INSTRUMENT FOR INTRODUCING THE SAME ABSOLUTE RULE INTO THESE COLONIES:

FOR TAKING AWAY OUR CHARTERS, ABOLISHING OUR MOST VALUABLE LAWS, AND ALTERING FUNDAMENTALLY THE FORMS OF OUR GOVERNMENTS:

FOR SUSPENDING OUR OWN LEGISLATURES, AND DECLARING THEMSELVES INVESTED WITH POWER TO LEGISLATE FOR US IN ALL CASES WHATSOEVER.

ROUND XIX · THE APPARATUS · The Same Overt Act

Raised under the First Amendment right of the people to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.

To every Senator and Representative, every elected and appointed member of the chain of command, at every level, and every civil officer down to state and local:

On November 16 the Warning asked one thing of you: read the law before taking this crusade against officials one step further without the requisites. It went unheeded. This is the Round it promised.

It names no one and charges no one. The power to charge, try, expel and remove sits with the offices below. To them we defer. None of them do we excuse. What follows is the apparatus itself, in the law's own words: the line for each office, the proof required before any officer is called across it, and the hand that holds the remedy. It cuts both ways. It spares neither the officer who crosses the line nor the officer who cries treason without the requisites.

I. THE OATH

One clause stands under every office here: "The Senators and Representatives before mentioned, and the Members of the several State Legislatures, and all executive and judicial Officers, both of the United States and of the several States, shall be bound by Oath or Affirmation, to support this Constitution" (Art. VI).

Every officer of the civil and uniformed services, "except the President," swears what that means: to "support and defend the Constitution of the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic," to "bear true faith and allegiance to the same," "without any mental reservation or purpose of evasion," and to "well and faithfully discharge the duties of the office" (5 U.S.C. 3331). The President swears his own: "to the best of my Ability, preserve, protect and defend the Constitution of the United States" (Art. II, §1).

The duties of the office. Not of a party, a caucus, a bureau or a foreign capital.

II. THE TOP OF THE SCALE: TREASON

The line: "Treason against the United States, shall consist only in levying War against them, or in adhering to their Enemies, giving them Aid and Comfort" (Art. III, §3). The word is "only." It is the only crime the Constitution defines.

The requisites:
"No Person shall be convicted of Treason unless on the Testimony of two Witnesses to the same overt Act, or on Confession in open Court."
Levying war is an act, not a plan: "To conspire to levy war, and actually to levy war, are distinct offences," and "there must be an actual assembling of men, for the treasonable purpose, to constitute a levying of war." Once men are so assembled, "all those who perform any part, however minute, or however remote from the scene of action, and who are actually leagued in the general conspiracy, are to be considered as traitors" (Ex parte Bollman, 1807).
Aid and comfort demands two things, both proved: adherence to the enemy, and an overt act by which the accused "actually gave aid and comfort to the enemy"; and "if there is no intent to betray, there is no treason" (Cramer v. United States, 1945).

The penalty, for whoever does it "owing allegiance to the United States": death, or not less than five years, and to be "incapable of holding any office under the United States" (18 U.S.C. 2381). The Constitution bounds it: "The Congress shall have Power to declare the Punishment of Treason, but no Attainder of Treason shall work Corruption of Blood, or Forfeiture except during the Life of the Person attainted" (Art. III, §3). To know of a treason, to conceal it and not make it known, is its own crime under the same allegiance: misprision, seven years (18 U.S.C. 2382).

Who holds it: a United States attorney, a grand jury and a court. Not a chamber: "No Bill of Attainder or ex post facto Law shall be passed" (Art. I, §9). Not a committee. Not a cable. Not a microphone.

That is the measure for every officer who throws the word at another. Bring the two witnesses, or put the word down. Where they stand, no office may look away.

III. BELOW TREASON: THE STATUTES THAT SAY "WHOEVER"

Insurrection. "Whoever incites, sets on foot, assists, or engages in any rebellion or insurrection against the authority of the United States or the laws thereof, or gives aid or comfort thereto": ten years, and "incapable of holding any office under the United States" (18 U.S.C. 2383).

Seditious conspiracy. If "two or more persons" conspire "by force to prevent, hinder, or delay the execution of any law of the United States": twenty years (18 U.S.C. 2384). The requisite is an agreement to use force. Without it there is no seditious conspiracy, and no officer may call it one.

The forces. "Whoever, with intent to interfere with, impair, or influence the loyalty, morale, or discipline of the military or naval forces," "advises, counsels, urges, or in any manner causes or attempts to cause insubordination, disloyalty, mutiny, or refusal of duty": ten years, and five years barred from federal employment (18 U.S.C. 2387). The requisite is intent. The word is "Whoever." It exempts no office.

The disability. No one who took the oath "as a member of Congress, or as an officer of the United States, or as a member of any State legislature, or as an executive or judicial officer of any State," and then "engaged in insurrection or rebellion against the same, or given aid or comfort to the enemies thereof," may hold any office, "civil or military, under the United States, or under any State" (Amend. XIV, §3). Only two thirds of each House can lift it. Its enforcement is the Congress's, "by appropriate legislation" (§5).

IV. THE OFFICES, EACH BY ITS OWN LINE

1. STATE, AND ITS AMBASSADORS
The charge: a chief of mission acts "Under the direction of the President" (22 U.S.C. 3927). It is the President who "shall receive Ambassadors and other public Ministers" (Art. II, §3).
The deviation: a line of one's own. The statute is written for "Any citizen of the United States, wherever he may be": to carry on, "without authority of the United States," any "correspondence or intercourse with any foreign government" with intent "to defeat the measures of the United States": three years (18 U.S.C. 953). It saves one right: the citizen's own claim "for redress of any injury" from that government or its people. No one "holding any Office of Profit or Trust under them," the United States, may accept, without the consent of the Congress, "any present, Emolument, Office, or Title, of any kind whatever, from any King, Prince, or foreign State" (Art. I, §9).
Who holds it: the President. For the "President, Vice President and all civil Officers of the United States," removal "on Impeachment for, and Conviction of, Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors" (Art. II, §4): the House has "the sole Power of Impeachment," the Senate "the sole Power to try." The judgment "shall not extend further than to removal from Office, and disqualification to hold and enjoy any Office of honor, Trust or Profit under the United States: but the Party convicted shall nevertheless be liable and subject to Indictment, Trial, Judgment and Punishment, according to Law."
@StateDept 

2. THE DEPARTMENT OF WAR, THE JOINT STAFF AND THE UNIFORMED CHAIN
The Declaration's count against the King: "He has affected to render the Military independent of and superior to the Civil power."
Among those reached: the regular forces; the Guard, "but only when in Federal service"; and "Retired members of a regular component of the armed forces who are entitled to pay" (10 U.S.C. 802).
The line, mutiny: "with intent to usurp or override lawful military authority, refuses, in concert with any other person, to obey orders or otherwise do his duty."
The line, sedition: "with intent to cause the overthrow or destruction of lawful civil authority, creates, in concert with any other person, revolt, violence, or other disturbance against that authority."
The line, silence: whoever "fails to do his utmost to prevent and suppress a mutiny or sedition being committed in his presence," or "fails to take all reasonable means to inform his superior commissioned officer or commanding officer of a mutiny or sedition which he knows or has reason to believe is taking place," is guilty beside them.
The penalty for all three: "death or such other punishment as a court-martial may direct" (10 U.S.C. 894).
The requisites: intent, always. Concert, for the refusal and for sedition. Mutiny by violence or disturbance "may be committed by one person acting alone." The intent "may be declared in words or inferred from acts, omissions, or surrounding circumstances" (Manual for Courts-Martial, 2024 ed., Part IV, para. 21).
"Any commissioned officer who uses contemptuous words against the President, the Vice President, Congress, the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of a military department, the Secretary of Homeland Security, or the Governor or legislature of any State, Commonwealth, or possession in which he is on duty or present shall be punished as a court-martial may direct" (10 U.S.C. 888). It guards the Congress as it guards the President. "Any person who" aids the enemy "with arms, ammunition, supplies, money, or other things," or "without proper authority, knowingly" gives the enemy intelligence or "holds any intercourse" with him, "shall suffer death or such other punishment" (10 U.S.C. 903b).
Who holds it: the court-martial, convened within the chain.
@DeptofWar @thejointstaff @USNationalGuard 

3. JUSTICE, AND EVERY CIVIL OFFICER
The charge: the President "shall take Care that the Laws be faithfully executed" (Art. II, §3), and the Department of Justice holds the charging power for everything in Parts II and III.
The deviation runs two ways. To loose that power without the requisites is persecution. To withhold it where they are met is protection. Neither is faithful execution.
The bar: no one may "accept or hold a position in the Government of the United States" who "advocates the overthrow of our constitutional form of government" (5 U.S.C. 7311); the breach is a crime, up to a year and a day (18 U.S.C. 1918).
Who holds it: the President over his officers; the House and the Senate by impeachment.
@TheJusticeDept

4. THE HOUSE AND THE SENATE
The line: "Each House may determine the Rules of its Proceedings, punish its Members for disorderly Behaviour, and, with the Concurrence of two thirds, expel a Member" (Art. I, §5). House Rule XXIII opens on the same standard: to behave at all times in a manner that shall "reflect creditably on the House."
The shield, and its edge: "for any Speech or Debate in either House, they shall not be questioned in any other Place." The words are "in either House." The privilege from arrest holds "in all Cases, except Treason, Felony and Breach of the Peace," and only "during their Attendance at the Session of their respective Houses, and in going to and returning from the same" (Art. I, §6). For treason and for felony there is none.
The record: the Senate has expelled fifteen: one in 1797, on a recorded ground of "Anti-Spanish conspiracy; treason," and fourteen in 1861 and 1862 for supporting the Confederacy. The House has expelled six: three in 1861 for taking up arms with the Confederacy, two after criminal convictions, in 1980 and 2002, and one by resolution in 2023.
Who holds it: each chamber, alone, over its own. No court, no President and no recall takes a seat between elections, and since 1799, though the Senate "failed to voice its opinion on that matter," its dismissal of the Blount case "set a precedent that still holds today": "a U.S. senator cannot be impeached" (IN CONGRESS ASSEMBLED, Count Seven). "Each House shall be the Judge of the Elections, Returns and Qualifications of its own Members" (Art. I, §5). That is why this Round is addressed to you first. The remedy is yours alone. So is the failure.
@HouseGOP @HouseDemocrats @SenateGOP @SenateDems 

5. THE GOVERNORS, THE GUARD UNDER STATE COMMAND, THE MAYORS, THE COUNTIES AND THE SHERIFFS
The oath is the same one: Article VI binds officers "both of the United States and of the several States." "This Constitution, and the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof; and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding."
The line: "No State shall enter into any Treaty, Alliance, or Confederation." Nor, "without the Consent of Congress," may it "keep Troops, or Ships of War in time of Peace, enter into any Agreement or Compact with another State, or with a foreign Power, or engage in War, unless actually invaded, or in such imminent Danger as will not admit of delay" (Art. I, §10).
The reach: Part III says "Whoever." The Fourteenth Amendment names the "executive or judicial officer of any State." The Guard under a governor stands outside the Uniform Code until Federal service puts it in.
Who holds it: each State's own constitution and courts; the federal courts under the supremacy clause; the Congress under the Fourteenth.
@NatlGovsAssoc @usmayors @leagueofcities @NACoCounties @NationalSheriff 

V. USURPATION, QUANTIFIED AND QUALIFIED

Standing law gives the word two homes.

An authority usurped. That is mutiny, set down above, done "with intent to usurp or override lawful military authority" (10 U.S.C. 894). The penalty runs to death.

An office usurped. Quo warranto is the writ for an office held without title: it may issue from the federal district court in Washington, in the name of the United States, against whoever "within the District of Columbia usurps, intrudes into, or unlawfully holds or exercises" a federal office, civil or military (D.C. Code 16-3501). Standing to bring it sits with the Attorney General or the United States attorney; on their refusal, the court may grant leave to an interested person who gives security for costs. The price of losing is the office: ouster and exclusion.

For a power taken by one branch from another, the remedies are the ones already set down: judgment in a case, expulsion, impeachment, and the ballot. Washington's Farewell: "let there be no change by usurpation; for though this, in one instance, may be the instrument of good, it is the customary weapon by which free governments are destroyed." Marshall's rule for his own bench is the rule for every office: "We have no more right to decline the exercise of jurisdiction which is given, than to usurp that which is not given. The one or the other would be treason to the constitution" (Cohens v. Virginia, 1821).

VI. THE FOREIGN HAND

The gift. Bribery reaches whoever "directly or indirectly, corruptly gives, offers or promises anything of value to any public official" with intent "to influence any official act," and the official who "directly or indirectly, corruptly demands, seeks, receives, accepts, or agrees to receive or accept anything of value personally or for any other person or entity" in return (18 U.S.C. 201). The statute's "public official" begins: "Member of Congress." The penalty: fifteen years, three times the value of the thing, and the convicted "may be disqualified from holding any office of honor, trust, or profit under the United States." The words are "directly or indirectly," on both sides of the table. A proxy does not clean the money. The requisites: corrupt intent, and one of three ends: an official act influenced, a fraud on the United States, or a breach of official duty.

The agent. "No person shall act as an agent of a foreign principal unless he has filed with the Attorney General a true and complete registration statement," or "is exempt from registration" (22 U.S.C. 612): five years for the willful breach (22 U.S.C. 618). The Act's agent is one who acts "at the order, request, or under the direction or control, of a foreign principal" in political, publicity, money or representation work within the United States (22 U.S.C. 611). Registration discloses the agent. It licenses nothing else. By the statute's own words, a filing shall not "indicate that the Attorney General has in any way passed upon the merits" (22 U.S.C. 612). No officer may be one, save a special Government employee whose agency head certifies the employment "is required in the national interest": "Whoever, being a public official, is or acts as an agent of a foreign principal required to register" answers with two years (18 U.S.C. 219), and there too "public official" begins "Member of Congress."

The sanctioned party. "It shall be unlawful for a person to violate, attempt to violate, conspire to violate, or cause a violation of any license, order, regulation, or prohibition issued under this chapter" (50 U.S.C. 1705): a civil penalty up to the greater of $250,000, adjusted each year for inflation (31 CFR 586.701), or "twice the amount of the transaction," and for the willful, up to one million dollars, twenty years, or both. A filed registration answers section 612. It does not answer section 1705. Where the principal is under sanction, the dealing the sanction forbids is the breach, whatever was filed, and money that reaches an officer through his agent is "indirectly" given.

The investment. For every "United States person," officers included, the standing order prohibits "the purchase or sale of any publicly traded securities" of the companies Treasury lists as China's military-industrial complex (E.O. 13959, as amended by E.O. 14032; 31 CFR 586), under the same penalties; the order permits sales "made solely to effect the divestment" for 365 days after a listing, and applies "except to the extent provided by statutes, or in regulations, orders, directives, or licenses." The Code's own list of a "covered nation," written "In this section" for defense procurement, names four: North Korea, China, Russia and Iran (10 U.S.C. 4872). A federal officer's interest in any foreign state's enterprise meets Article I, §9 first: no "Emolument" from any "foreign State" without the consent of the Congress. An executive officer who "participates personally and substantially" in a matter in which, "to his knowledge," he "has a financial interest" answers under 18 U.S.C. 208, unless the section's own exemptions cover him. "Subject to the rule of construction under section 10 of the STOCK Act and solely for purposes of the insider trading prohibitions," each Member of Congress "owes a duty arising from a relationship of trust and confidence to the Congress, the United States Government, and the citizens of the United States" over the "material, nonpublic information" his office gives him; the same section lays a like duty, "to the United States Government and the citizens of the United States," on "each executive branch employee, each judicial officer, and each judicial employee," the President and the Vice President by name (15 U.S.C. 78u-1).

The harbored. An agent of a foreign power, in the surveillance statute's words, includes any person who "knowingly engages in clandestine intelligence gathering activities for or on behalf of a foreign power, which activities involve or may involve a violation of the criminal statutes of the United States" (50 U.S.C. 1801). "Whoever harbors or conceals any person who he knows, or has reasonable grounds to believe or suspect, has committed, or is about to commit, an offense under sections 793 or 794 of this title," in the espionage chapter, answers with ten years (18 U.S.C. 792). Whoever, "having knowledge of the actual commission of a felony cognizable by a court of the United States," "conceals and does not as soon as possible make known the same" answers with three (18 U.S.C. 4). The head of an agency the statute lists may suspend, and then, "Subject to subsection (c)," remove an employee of his agency "in the interests of national security"; subsection (c) first gives the permanent citizen employee, past probation, written charges, an answer, a hearing and a review; then "The determination of the head of the agency is final" (5 U.S.C. 7531, 7532).

The requisites are knowledge, or reasonable grounds; and harboring, or concealing. To have been deceived is not the crime. To be told, and then to keep, to shelter or to conceal, is where the statute begins.

VII. THE COURTS THAT CAN PUNISH

From open sources alone: the statute book, and the Court's own reports.

The district courts. Every Title 18 felony in this Round is tried there, on indictment, before a jury. So, since 2024, are the Commission's fraud penalties: "The Seventh Amendment therefore applies and a jury is required" (SEC v. Jarkesy).

The Senate, on impeachments, and each House, over its own. Set down above.

The courts-martial: general, special and summary (10 U.S.C. 816). Above them, a Court of Criminal Appeals under each Judge Advocate General (10 U.S.C. 866). Above those, the Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces, "established under article I of the Constitution" (10 U.S.C. 941). Above that, the Supreme Court, by certiorari, in the four classes of case the statute lists (28 U.S.C. 1259).

The military commission. "Any alien unprivileged enemy belligerent is subject to trial by military commission" (10 U.S.C. 948c). The alien. Not the citizen.

The surveillance court. "11 district court judges," publicly designated by the Chief Justice, "hear applications for and grant orders approving electronic surveillance"; three more sit as its court of review (50 U.S.C. 1803). It tries no one. It opens the door to the evidence. It has an edge of its own: the officer who "intentionally engages in electronic surveillance under color of law except as authorized" is guilty of a crime, ten years, with a defense for the officer on duty where the surveillance "was authorized by and conducted pursuant to a search warrant or court order of a court of competent jurisdiction" (50 U.S.C. 1809). The officer or employee "who engages in intentional misconduct with respect to proceedings before" it or its court of review "shall be subject to appropriate adverse actions, including, at minimum, suspension without pay or removal" (50 U.S.C. 1803).

The removal court. "5 district court judges," designated the same way, with "jurisdiction to conduct all removal proceedings" against alien terrorists (8 U.S.C. 1532).

The Commission. In the proceedings the statute names, the SEC "may impose a civil penalty if it finds, on the record after notice and opportunity for hearing, that such penalty is in the public interest," in its own house (15 U.S.C. 78u-2).

The Treasury. Under section 1705, "A civil penalty may be imposed on any person," and it is the Department's own office that imposes it.

The agency head, where the statute lists the agency. Suspension and removal, as set down in Part VI (5 U.S.C. 7531, 7532).

And "that" one. It is not charted here. It does not need to be.

What sits behind those benches is deferred, without contest, to those who hold it.

VIII. THE NUMBERS

Two witnesses to the same overt act. Two thirds to expel. Two thirds of the Senators present to convict on impeachment. Two thirds of each House to lift the Fourteenth's disability. Three years for dealing with a foreign government without authority. Seven for hiding a treason. Ten for insurrection, and ten for working on the loyalty of the forces. Twenty for seditious conspiracy. Not less than five, or death, for treason. Death, or as a court-martial may direct, for mutiny, for sedition in uniform, and for aiding the enemy. Fifteen for the bribe, given or taken. Five for the unregistered agent, and two for the officer who is one. Twenty for the willful breach of a sanction. Ten for harboring a spy. Ten for the unlawful wiretap. Every term of years in this Round is the statute's ceiling, "not more than," and each stands beside a fine, "or both." Treason alone carries a floor.

None of this is new, and none of it is ours. It is the law and the record, as the Government's own press prints it. Read it before the next step. Weigh the officer you accuse by it. Then weigh yourself.

Whatever your office, you all swore an oath. The faithful execution of LEGITIMATELY CHARGED DUTIES, under the supremacy of U.S. sovereignty, is what those offices are for: elected, appointed, or otherwise vested under the law of the land.

Cross any line above, and you are unfit for the trust you hold. Shield the one who does, and you stand beside him. Cry treason without the requisites, and you stand with both.

We hold no office and we set no terms. Judgment and action belong to the offices that alone can charge, try, expel or remove. The remedies that are the People's are lawful, and we SHALL use them: the ballot, Article V, and the petition.

We the People

I built the app I needed. Today, @kizunoapp is live. 🎉

For years I've been running communities for different startups I've built. On top of that, I'm a member of plenty of communities myself: local groups, clubs, places I go to every week.

And every single one ran on something different.
One lived in a WhatsApp group. Another in a spreadsheet. Another on paper punch cards that always got lost. As a member, I had a dozen apps and cards to keep track of. As an organiser, I was juggling tools that were never built for communities in the first place.

So I started building something in my spare time when I don't work on deep tech. It started as a side project, partly to fix the problem for myself and manage my own communities in one place. And partly because I knew I couldn't be the only one dealing with this.
That side project became Kizuno.

If you're a member, it's one free app for all your communities. Collect points with a QR code, chat with the group, vote on decisions and get entered into giveaways.

If you run a community, you choose only what you need from 14+ modules (more on the way): points, stamp cards, rewards, events, leaderboards, voting, analytics and more. A running club and a café shouldn't need the same app, so every community on Kizuno looks the way its owner wants.
It's free to create a community, then a flat €29/month to activate it.

🎁 Launch offer for community owners: your first 2 months are completely free, with no card and no application.
